newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela sets 100 bln bolivar TEM auction Wed.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela sets 100 bln bolivar TEM auction Wed.

text.p: The Central Bank of Venezuela announced for Wednesday morning a 60 billion bolivar ($126 million) auction of 178-day "monetary stabilization," or TEM, bills with a 16.09 percent coupon.
The bank said it would also offer 20 billion bolivars ($42 million) in 267-day bills with a 16.41 percent coupon, and another 20 billion bolivars of 358-day bills with a 16.74 percent coupon.
Some 16 billion bolivars of TEMs are due to mature on Thursday.

Coupons at the Wednesday auction are down from last week's 100 billion bolivar issue. Then 178-, 267- and 358-day notes carried 18.16, 18.56, and 18.98 percent coupons respectively for effective yields that softened to 16.09, 17.42 and 18.32 percent.
The weekly TEM bill auctions are the Central Bank's principal tool of monetary policy, used to restrict liquidity and establish a benchmark for wider interest rates.
